title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed Bourbaki editorial report, 'SYSTÈMES de RACINES (5), Tribu n° 59'. It sits inside the folder of handwritten notes on motives and Hodge theory, probably as scrap paper or by misfiling; the neighbouring pages are handwritten notes on fibre functors on motives over fields isomorphic to C or R. The page records editorial decisions for the drafting of Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, ch. VI (root systems).

Editorial items:
- A remark that the reflection in a simple root v_i sends v_i to -v_i and permutes the other positive roots.
- A request to add a lemma on maps R -> groups, which looks like the preparation for the Coxeter/Weyl group presentation.
- Sections 6 and 7 are swapped, so the new n°6 is 'closed sets of roots'.
- Serre's Prop. 4 and Prop. 5 from Bourbaki redaction n°400, Annexe II, are to be added; Serre's corollary and Lemma 2 become exercises.
- For Prop. 15 a proof supplied by Borel is adopted.

Prop. 15 is essentially what appears in the published Lie VI §1.7 (Prop. 22): if P is a closed subset of a root system R (x, y ∈ P and x+y ∈ R imply x+y ∈ P) with P ∩ (-P) = ∅, then P is contained in the set of positive roots for some chamber.

Borel's proof, steps 1–3:
1) Two proportional roots in P have positive ratio. Proportional roots have ratio ±1/2, ±1 or ±2, and -1 is excluded by P ∩ -P = ∅. So one may assume x = -y/2. Then x + y = y/2 is a root, so by closedness y/2 ∈ P, while -y/2 = x ∈ P, a contradiction. Combined with the standard fact (Prop. 4 of n°3) that (x,y) < 0 for non-opposite roots implies x+y ∈ R, this gives: x, y ∈ P and (x,y) < 0 imply x+y ∈ P.
2) No sum y_1 + … + y_q of elements of P vanishes. The proof is by induction on q. If the sum is 0, then -y_1 = y_2 + … + y_q, so (y_1, y_2 + … + y_q) = -|y_1|^2 < 0. Hence some j ≥ 2 has (y_1, y_j) < 0, so y_1 + y_j ∈ P, and replacing y_1, y_j by their sum gives a vanishing sum of q-1 elements.
3) The page begins to show there is z ≠ 0 with (z,x) ≥ 0 for all x ∈ P, arguing by contradiction (a Farkas/Gordan-type alternative). The proof continues on the next typed page, which is not given here.

The argument is correct and standard.
errors: In step 2 the hypothesis should read 'Si y_1 + … + y_q = 0'; as transcribed ('y_1 + y_q = 0') it is a typo or transcription slip.
The index j should range over 2 ≤ j ≤ q, not 1 ≤ j ≤ q, since (y_1, y_1) > 0. This is harmless.
Step 1 implicitly uses that in a (possibly non-reduced) root system proportional roots have ratio in {±1/2, ±1, ±2}. This is standard.

ideas.what: A closed subset P of a root system with P ∩ -P = ∅ lies in some positive system; Borel's proof via the non-vanishing of sums and a separating-hyperplane argument
ideas.modern_name: Closed symmetric-free subsets of roots lie in a positive system (Bourbaki Lie VI §1.7 Prop. 22)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bourbaki (proof attributed internally to A. Borel); related results in Borel–Tits
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, ch. VI §1 n°7 (1968)

ideas.what: A simple reflection permutes the positive roots other than its own root

deep.surprise_reason: This is a misfiled or reused Bourbaki Tribu typescript on root systems, not Grothendieck's mathematics. Its only interest is archival: it attests that Borel supplied the proof of the closed-subset proposition and documents Bourbaki's editorial decisions. Both are of minor historical interest and the result itself is published.
transcription_corrections: 'Si y_1 + y_q = 0' should read 'Si y_1 + … + y_q = 0' (the ellipsis is faint or omitted in the typescript).
The page is a typed Bourbaki document ('Tribu n° 59'), not part of the handwritten motives notes; the '27' at the bottom is the archive's pencil foliation.
